newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakhstan sees 1997 crude exports rising near 50%.
newsitem.headline: Kazakhstan sees 1997 crude exports rising near 50%.

text.p: Kazakhstan plans to boost crude oil exports to 13-14 million tonnes (260,000-280,000 barrels per day) in 1997 from nine million tonnes (180,000 bpd) last year, Kazakhoil chairman Nurlan Balgimbayev said on Thursday.

"The Kazakh economy will win a lot from higher oil exports," he told a news conference, adding that 10 million tonnes (200,000 bpd) would go to countries outside the Commonwealth of Independent States.

Balgimbayev said seven million tonnes (140,000 bpd) would be exported this year through a pipeline across Russia, while one million tonnes (20,000 bpd) would be shipped by tankers across the Caspian Sea to the Azeri capital of Baku.
Kazakhstan -- a resource-rich but landlocked former Soviet republic -- also plans to export one million tonnes (20,000 bpd) this year through swaps with Iran.
Balgimbayev said the first swap would take place by April 15.
Under the scheme, Kazakhstan will ship its oil across the Caspian to Iran's Caspian coast. In turn, Iran will make available the same amount of crude at its Persian Gulf ports.
Balgimbayev said another one million tonnes (20,000 bpd) would be delivered to Europe by railway, adding that in the second half of this year, Kazakhstan would ship oil by rail to western China.
Kazakhstan aims to boost oil output from 26.5 million tonnes (530,000 bpd) this year to 170 million tonnes (3.4 million bpd) by 2010.
Balgimbayev said the Central Asian country had reserves of over three billion tonnes (21.9 billion barrels).
